subject: Biology
description: Tropical forest, savanna, desert, taiga, tundra, grassland — climate, flora, fauna

questions.stem: The TROPICAL RAINFOREST biome is characterised by:

options.option_text: Cold winters, short summers, evergreen conifers dominant
High year-round temperature, very high rainfall, rich biodiversity
Hot summers, cold winters, deep grass cover, few trees
Sparse vegetation, large day-night temperature range, low rainfall

questions.explanation: Tropical rainforest: 25-30 °C year round, > 200 cm rainfall, multi-storeyed canopy, MOST biodiverse biome (~50% of world species in <10% of land area). Examples: Amazon, Congo, SE Asia, Western Ghats. Distractor 1 = taiga / boreal. Distractor 3 = temperate grassland (prairie, steppe). Distractor 4 = desert.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The world's LARGEST TERRESTRIAL biome by area is the:

options.option_text: Tropical rainforest of South America
Taiga (boreal forest) of the northern hemisphere
Savanna grassland of central Africa
Hot desert belt of subtropical latitudes

questions.explanation: Taiga (boreal forest) — wraps a near-continuous belt across northern Russia, Scandinavia, Canada, Alaska. ~17 million km² (largest land biome). Dominant trees: spruce, pine, fir, larch (all conifers). Cold winters (down to −40 °C), short summers, low species diversity but immense biomass. Stores ~30% of world's terrestrial carbon → critical for climate. Tropical rainforest ~14 million km² (2nd). Hot deserts cover ~14% of land. Savanna ~13%.

questions.stem: The TUNDRA biome is distinguished by:

options.option_text: Tall coniferous forest with thick organic soil
Permanently frozen subsoil (permafrost) and very short summers
Heavy summer monsoon and dense seasonal grass
Hot dry climate with cactus and thorn vegetation

questions.explanation: Tundra — Arctic regions (Russia, Canada, Alaska, Scandinavia), and high alpine zones. Permafrost prevents deep root growth, so dwarf shrubs, mosses, lichens dominate (no tall trees). Short growing season (~2 months). Migratory wildlife: caribou, reindeer, arctic fox, polar bear, musk ox, snow geese. Permafrost thaw releases methane + CO₂ — major climate-change feedback. Distractor 1 = taiga. Distractor 3 = monsoon-fed grassland. Distractor 4 = hot desert.

questions.stem: The SAVANNA biome (e.g., Serengeti) is best described as:

options.option_text: Continuous dense forest with closed canopy and high humidity
Tropical grassland with scattered trees, alternating wet-dry seasons
Permanently frozen plain with mosses and dwarf shrubs
Dry sandy expanse where rainfall is below 25 cm a year

questions.explanation: Savanna — tropical grassland with widely spaced trees (acacia, baobab). Distinct wet (~50 cm) and dry seasons, regular fires that maintain grassland (suppress forest invasion). Famous for large-mammal herds: wildebeest, zebra, giraffe, elephant, lion, cheetah. Locations: African Serengeti, Brazilian cerrado, Australian savanna, parts of India (Terai-Duar). Distractor 1 = tropical rainforest. Distractor 3 = tundra. Distractor 4 = desert.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Cacti, succulents, and xerophytic shrubs are the dominant vegetation of which biome?

options.option_text: Mediterranean shrubland of southern Europe
Hot desert biome (Sahara, Kalahari, Thar)
Temperate deciduous forest of eastern USA
Tropical evergreen forest of equatorial Africa

questions.explanation: Hot desert — < 25 cm rainfall, large day-night temperature swings, plants adapt with thick stems for water storage (cactus), waxy cuticles, deep roots, reduced leaves. Famous deserts: Sahara (largest hot desert), Arabian, Kalahari, Atacama (driest), Thar (India-Pakistan), Mojave, Sonoran. Cold deserts also exist — Gobi, Patagonian, Antarctic (largest desert overall). Distractor 1 — Mediterranean has shrubs but in milder climate (chaparral / maquis). Distractor 3 — broadleaf trees (oak, maple). Distractor 4 — closed-canopy rainforest.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Temperate DECIDUOUS forests, dominant in eastern North America and central Europe, are characterised by trees that:

options.option_text: Stay evergreen with needle-shaped leaves all year
Shed their broad leaves seasonally before winter starts
Grow only as scrubby bushes due to constant grazing
Trap moisture using thick waxy cuticles in dry summers

questions.explanation: Temperate deciduous forest — broadleaf trees (oak, maple, beech, birch) that drop leaves before winter to conserve water (frozen ground = no uptake). Four distinct seasons; striking autumn colours. Found in eastern USA, western + central Europe, eastern China, Japan, parts of Himalayas. Soil is rich (leaf litter decomposes well). Distractor 1 = boreal (taiga). Distractor 3 = grazed shrubland. Distractor 4 = Mediterranean (sclerophyllous / chaparral).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The biome that lies BETWEEN the tundra and the temperate deciduous forest is the:

options.option_text: Tropical savanna grassland of the equator
Taiga or boreal coniferous forest belt
Subtropical hot desert near 30° latitude
Mediterranean shrubland of mild coasts

questions.explanation: Latitude bands from poles to equator (rough): TUNDRA (Arctic) → TAIGA (subarctic) → TEMPERATE DECIDUOUS FOREST (mid-latitudes) → SUBTROPICAL DESERTS (~30°N/S) → SAVANNA → TROPICAL RAINFOREST (equator). The taiga is the cold-but-tree-tolerating belt directly south of the tundra, marked by a 'tree line' boundary at the north. Distractor 1 — tropical, not subarctic. Distractor 3 — at ~30° latitude. Distractor 4 — at ~40° in narrow coastal bands.
